sources.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning, annotated
sources.snippet: Architecture: a way to join a pretrained, frozen vision model to a pretrained, frozen language model, to handle any interleaving of pictures and text, and to take images or video as input. Data: training on web pages with images scattered through the text, plus image-caption and video-caption pairs, and no data annotated for machine learning.

sources.title: Multimodal Architectures - Flamingo - Course notes
sources.snippet: Lecture: Flamingo - Interleaved Vision-Language Modeling Introduction Flamingo is a family of multimodal few-shot learners Developed by DeepMind Flamingo is a generative model that can process and generate sequences of interleaved images and text. This differs from CLIP, which performs retrieval or classification in latent space.

sources.title: Flamingo Explained: Few-Shot Learning for Vision-Language Understanding
sources.snippet: In "Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning" by Jean-Baptiste Alayrac and colleagues at DeepMind, the authors push vision-language models into the few-shot world. Flamingo can answer image-based questions, describe videos, or even do multimodal reasoning without fine-tuning—just by seeing a handful of examples in its context.
